caveats: The enterprise-count universe (sbs_sc_ovw) covers 2021-2024 only. Indicator values outside that window have no denominator and cannot be converted to absolute numbers.

The ICT surveys' sector total (C10-S951_X_K) and the SBS business-economy total (B-S_X_O_S94) are different populations, not different labels. Absolute figures derived from this join are estimates, not exact counts.
The ICT surveys only sample enterprises with 10 or more employees. Micro-enterprises exist in the universe but are never measured, so any 'SME' figure here excludes them.
isoc_eb_ain2 uses bespoke NACE groupings that do not exist in the SBS universe, so sector rows are largely unweighted. Sector percentages are unaffected.

Size classes overlap; they are not a partition. SME_10_249 already contains SMALL_10_49 and MEDIUM_50_249, and ALL_GE10 contains those plus LARGE_GE250. Summing across size_emp double-counts. The same applies to indicators: a firm using three AI technologies is counted once in E_AI_TANY and three times across the individual technology indicators.

Every value is a percentage, but of 18 different base populations (see each unit's `base`). PC_ENT is a share of all enterprises; PC_ENT_AI_EC is a share only of those that considered AI. Both render as 0-100 and look comparable. Only compare or chart values that share the same base.

enterprise_count counts all enterprises, so only unit PC_ENT (`weightable: true`) may be multiplied by it to obtain absolute figures. Weighting any other unit produces a number with no meaning, because its base population is not the one being counted.
